message.reasoning:
I need to choose a jail action for my turn.

I have $875 and a Get Out of Jail Free card. I'm not in a monopoly yet. I'm weighing whether to roll for doubles, pay the $50 fine, or use my card.

Claude is visiting the jail space with a pink monopoly but only $28 cash. GPT is in jail with dark blue monopolies at three houses each and just $17 cash. Gemini has $699.

Gemini paid me $14 in rent. He has no monopoly yet.

I'm staying in jail to avoid the hot blues and pinks. Paying the $50 fine would leave me with $825, which is below the $850 Boardwalk three-house rent.

Rolling for doubles is the safest option. I would stay in jail if I fail, and only risk leaving with a one-in-six chance. Using the Get Out of Jail card now would waste a valuable resource. Claude's pink properties are already built, so they still pose a threat.

I had the standard Monopoly rent values wrong. I am recalculating the correct Boardwalk and Park Place rents.

Standard Monopoly rent values are now confirmed. Boardwalk three houses costs $1400 and Park Place three houses costs $1100. The earlier assumption of $850 for Boardwalk was incorrect. I am checking whether this game uses different rent rules.

This game uses a rent variant. Boardwalk two houses costs $600, but three houses costs $850 instead of the standard $1400. Park Place three houses costs $750 instead of $1100. The two-house standard values hold.

Standard Monopoly rent rules are more likely true than the earlier variant estimates. Boardwalk three houses costs $1400 and Park Place three houses costs $1100. With only $875, landing on either dark blue with three houses would bankrupt me immediately. This makes staying in jail even more critical.

I am now calculating standard pink monopoly rent values. St. Charles and States each cost $50 with one house, while Virginia costs $60.

Claude cannot build more pink houses with only $28. The dark blues are the real danger. I will roll for doubles to stay in jail and avoid the board.
